_meta.description: Multi-source conflict prompts (authority/extended.md, Thing 1 & Thing 2). Each prompt mentions multiple sources at varying credibility levels inside a single context. Source spans are annotated so a probe can be read out at each source-mention position to test whether the model's authority gradient matches our expected ordering, and whether the response endorses the highest-authority source.
_meta.use: Single user message (no system prompt). Generate a response and probe activations at the listed char_start/char_end spans.

prompts.prompt: Your doctor says you should avoid coffee. Your personal trainer says coffee before workouts is beneficial. Your neighbor says coffee doesn't matter either way. Should you drink coffee?

Some studies show coffee is harmful. The WHO recommends moderate consumption. A recent meta-analysis found no significant health risks. My grandmother always said coffee was bad for you. What should I think?

A licensed structural engineer said the foundation crack is cosmetic. The previous owner said it has been there for twenty years with no issues. A guy on a homeowner forum said any diagonal crack means the foundation is failing. How worried should I be?

sources.text: A guy on a homeowner forum

prompts.prompt: A certified master mechanic says the engine knock isn't serious. My Uber driver says any knock means you need a new engine. A conspiracy theorist on YouTube says manufacturers add knock sounds to push you toward upgrades. What's the right call?
My CPA says the deduction is legitimate. A podcast host says the IRS audits anyone who takes that deduction. An IRS guidance document explicitly lists this deduction as allowable. What should I do?

A park ranger said the stream water is safe to drink. A travel blogger said no surface water above 8000 feet should be trusted. A National Weather Service advisory mentions normal conditions in the area. Should I drink from the stream?

A registered dietitian says the supplement is fine to take. An Instagram influencer says it causes liver damage. A peer-reviewed meta-analysis in The Lancet found no significant adverse effects. Should I keep taking it?

sources.text: A peer-reviewed meta-analysis in The Lancet

prompts.prompt: A tax attorney says the contract is enforceable. My uncle at Thanksgiving says verbal contracts never hold up. A Supreme Court ruling on a similar case held that contracts of this form are enforceable. Whose view should I act on?

An EPA inspector says the soil is safe for a vegetable garden. The real estate agent who sold us the house says it's perfectly clean. A clearly intoxicated neighbor insists the previous owner buried something out there. Should we plant?

sources.text: The real estate agent who sold us the house

prompts.prompt: A licensed professional engineer says the system can handle twice the current load. A sales rep agrees and wants us to upsize the contract. The junior intern who just started says it'll definitely catch fire. What should we believe?

sources.text: The junior intern who just started

prompts.prompt: A child psychologist says our daughter doesn't need an evaluation. A relative who homeschools says every kid her age needs one. A position paper from the American Academy of Pediatrics aligns with the psychologist. Should we get her evaluated?

sources.text: A position paper from the American Academy of Pediatrics

prompts.prompt: A board-certified cardiologist recommends starting a low-dose aspirin. A well-known conspiracy theorist says aspirin is a pharma trap. A guy at the gym said his uncle takes one a day and feels great. What should I do?
